A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMI-based dataset-distillation work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite pagination and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of CMI-enhanced distillation, including benchmark accuracies, cross-architecture generalization, ablations, training curves, and computational costs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds proxy-architecture experiments reporting CMI values and classification accuracies in Tables 10–11.

M1.justification: The empirical CMI estimator, regularized objective, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The explicit reference to multiple pretrained teachers clarifies network sampling already described in v1 Section 4.3. Single-model perturbation is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate dataset distillation for image classification on SVHN, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K. The added architecture study reuses CIFAR-10 at IPC=10 and introduces no new dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–9 is unchanged, including MIM4DD, SeqMatch, IID, DREAM, PDD, and SDC. The additional proxy architectures are ablation settings; newly cited DWA and generative methods are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.6 adds an evaluation protocol for DM and DSA using four pretrained proxy architectures on CIFAR-10 at IPC=10, recording initial and final CMI with and without regularization alongside accuracy. Existing benchmark protocols are retained. The revised ImageNet resolution description does not establish changed preprocessing.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.6 and Tables 10–11 extend the narrower proxy-architecture analysis in Table 7. They examine ConvNet, AlexNet, VGG11, and ResNet18 for DM and DSA, relating architecture characteristics to CMI reduction and accuracy. Existing sensitivity, efficiency, and visualization analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both retain the five-repetition statements in Sections 5.1 and 5.3 and the uncertainty-reporting format of existing tables. New Tables 10–11 provide point estimates without introducing additional run-count information, uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises SVHN IPC=1 accuracy for IDM+CMI from 66.9±0.3 to 66.4±0.3 and IDC+CMI from 70.3±0.5 to 70.0±0.5, updating their improvement entries accordingly. Tables 10–11 add architecture-specific CMI measurements and accuracies. Other existing tables and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Markov-chain assumptions, CMI derivation, and Equations (1)–(11) are unchanged. The added discussion of architecture and feature dimensionality is empirical interpretation, without a new theorem, proof, or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: CMI measures class-aware complexity, provides a general distillation regularizer, and improves accuracy and training efficiency. The stated improvement of up to 5.5% and broad applicability claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 newly interprets CMI magnitude as more affected by feature dimensionality than network depth and qualifies clustering comparisons by dimensionality. Appendix A.7 explicitly acknowledges substantial overhead from multiple pretrained teachers and suggests model perturbation as future mitigation. Existing proxy-selection and IPC=1 limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract, clarifies the use of multiple pretrained ResNet18 teachers in Section 5.1, and documents proxy depths and feature dimensions in Tables 10–11. The teacher clarification is consistent with v1's existing sampling description.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cazenavette et al. (2023), Du et al. (2025), and two Zhong et al. (2024) works to support discussion of generative distillation and teacher perturbation. The principal related-work discussion and positioning against existing methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include limited wording edits, updated author affiliation/contact information and publication header, acknowledgments, an added architecture-ablation subsection, and a separately numbered limitations subsection. The visualization appendix moves from A.6 to A.8; the main narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds two side-by-side architecture-ablation tables, relocates Tables 2–3, and redistributes existing appendix visualizations across pages. Figures 1–11 retain their graphical content; the remaining changes are limited spacing and pagination adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added architecture study extends the earlier analysis of proxy choice, while the expanded limitations make teacher overhead more transparent. The code-access statement and implementation clarification also improve documentation. These are limited gains: the method and principal evidence remain stable, and the new ablation is confined to CIFAR-10 at IPC=10 with no reported uncertainty.
